verdict:
ESCALATE on three independent mandatory triggers - discordant benches, an ADVANCE outcome (blue's gated quarter-STARTER), and self-reported broken verification at both benches - plus the filed PRINCIPAL QUESTION, which the bench record does not answer. Named unresolved item for the escalation: THE ADMINISTRATION'S ACTUAL 2026 PSPA POSTURE FROM PRIMARY SOURCES. Nothing in either bench filing establishes it.

=== PART 1: THE PRINCIPAL QUESTION - VARIANTS x CLOCK ===

The question filed 8/14 is whether the administration can privatize the GSEs against a forecasted Democratic House. The mechanism answer is YES on the administrative path, and the court record does not engage with it at all. Both benches treated GSE reform as a single undifferentiated risk factor: red scored it SIZING/TIMING ('privatized GSEs = higher risk pricing on DUS,' magnitude PLAUSIBLE only) and blue called it 'the real contested leg... direction on DUS economics genuinely unmodeled.' Neither enumerated variants; neither priced a clock. That is the gap this draft must close, and it cannot be closed from the record - only framed.

MECHANISM. Conservatorship exit is FHFA-director authority under HERA plus a Treasury PSPA amendment. Both are EXECUTIVE actions. No House majority blocks either. What a Democratic House does kill is explicit-guarantee LEGISLATION - and that is the good branch for a DUS lender, not the bad one. The naive reading ('divided government blocks privatization, therefore GSE risk recedes') is WRONG-SIGNED for WD. A House flip does not reduce regime risk; it SELECTS WHICH BRANCH IS OPERATIVE, and it selects the worse one.

THE THREE VARIANTS, ranked by their effect on WD's DUS economics:

(a) ADMINISTRATIVE RELEASE WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT GUARANTEE - House-proof, and the variant a Dem House makes operative by elimination. Transmission to WD: guarantee ambiguity widens agency multifamily MBS spreads; wider spreads raise multifamily mortgage rates and cut origination volumes (WD's fee engine); separately, a privatizing Fannie repricing counterparty risk demands more first-loss or higher g-fees from DUS lenders, which directly taxes the risk-sharing economics on the $69.5B at-risk book. FHFA could simultaneously raise DUS lender capital/collateral requirements. Partial offset: higher rates extend MSR duration and slow runoff, so servicing value rises as origination falls. Net: WORSE, and it hits the fee engine that carries the equity story. THIS IS THE BRANCH THE COURT SHOULD HAVE PRICED AND DID NOT.

(b) NEGOTIATED RELEASE WITH A LEGISLATED EXPLICIT GUARANTEE - requires Congress; dies if the House flips. Best branch for WD: spread stability, volumes preserved, loss-sharing economics substantially unchanged, and the overhang lifts. Note the asymmetry that makes this the whole point of the principal question: this is the ONLY variant a Dem House can block, and it is the only variant that is good for WD.

(c) STATUS QUO DRIFT - conservatorship persists, FHFA continues administering caps ($88B per enterprise for 2026 with 50% mission-driven). Neutral to mildly positive for WD: the caps already constrain conventional multifamily volume, and the current DUS economics are the ones in the numbers.

CLOCK, AND WHY IT IS THE ACTIVE VARIABLE. Midterms November 2026; the new House seats 2027-01-03. If the administration's own forecast is a Democratic House, the rational move is to lock PSPA amendments and FHFA release actions BEFORE January - not after. That front-loads variant (a)'s spread-widening into September-December 2026, which is exactly (i) the window in which blue wants to seat a starter, (ii) the window containing WD's Q3 print (~11/5), and (iii) the window containing FHFA's 2027 multifamily cap announcement (historically November). A Dem-House forecast is therefore an ACCELERANT on the bad branch, not a brake on the whole process. The court's implicit framing - regime risk as a slow, undated, magnitude-unknown overhang - is the wrong shape. The right shape is a dated, front-loaded, variant-selecting sequence in which the desk's entry window and the acceleration window coincide.

WHAT THE RECORD ACTUALLY CONTAINS ON THIS. Red: FHFA 2026 caps (primary, FHFA news release) plus a '$30B GSE IPO' plan sourced to Multi-Housing News (SECONDARY). Blue: 'CONFIRMED live, magnitude PLAUSIBLE only.' There is NO primary read of: the current PSPA text or any 2026 amendment; Treasury's senior-preferred posture; the FHFA director's stated conservatorship-exit sequencing; whether any capital-raise registration exists. Neither bench mentions the guarantee question, the House-proof administrative path, or the pre-January acceleration. The principal question is UNADDRESSED, and it is decisive precisely because WD's DUS economics differ sharply across (a) and (b).

=== PART 2: THE BENCH DISPUTE ===

BLUE WON THE TWO DECISIVE EXCHANGES. Red's FATAL was the $14.4B maximum DUS contingent liability set against the thesis's ~$220M 'cap.' Blue found the same 10-Q note shows $14.1B in the prior period - static, decade-old first-loss boilerplate that was unchanged at $90/share. A number that did not move cannot be what repriced the stock. The same note gives a historical loss rate of 0.3bp and an allowance of $49.1M (~7bp). FATAL correctly reduced to SIZING. Red's category-error argument (a bounded cohort loss cannot explain a permanent multiple repricing) survives on its own logic - but its quantum does not. This is the III precedent for the third time in this batch.

Red's second kill - that the February break was an 'earnings-power event,' not a fraud event - is OVERTURNED by the vetted Q4'25 8-K: revenue was FLAT at $340.0M and volume was +36%, with the decline attributed to 'indemnified and repurchased loan expenses and asset impairments' ($35.8M fraud-loan expenses + $26.1M impairments). Blue bridges $0.28 -> ~$1.22 via the non-added-back ~$42M pre-tax (~$0.94/sh after tax), which satisfies red's own change-my-mind (c). CAUTION FOR THE ESCALATION: this bridge is the single finding that flips the verdict, it was PROXY-FETCHED, and my own check of the arithmetic is only approximate ($42M pre-tax at ~25% tax over ~35.7M shares gives ~$0.88, not $0.94 - reconcilable via tax rate and share count, but it must be re-derived from the primary 8-K, not accepted). Per the escalate-intelligence-on-decisive-findings rule, a load-bearing finding that reverses a court gets re-verified with full context before anyone acts on it.

Red was also FACTUALLY WRONG on venue: blue found the vetted Q2'26 8-K DOES contain 'we concluded that investigation with Freddie Mac, and we do not expect any further repurchases,' with Fannie reviews 'nearing the conclusion.' Red's claim that no no-repurchase commitment exists in vetted documents fails. Half of red's venue finding stands: the Q3 $12-16M charge guide and the $50.7M / Q4-2027 forbearance language are absent from BOTH the 10-Q and the 8-K, i.e. transcript-only and still unverified.

WHAT SURVIVES FOR RED, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING. The adjusted-core circularity is CONFIRMED by both benches: 'adjusted core' excludes 'provision for credit losses, net write-offs... loan repurchase losses' - the exact damage class in dispute - so citing $1.19 as proof of containment is circular. GAAP $0.09 against a $0.68 dividend; cash $299.3M -> $160.9M in H1 against ~$820.9M of corporate notes. Blue's mitigant (the Q2'25 gap was only $1.15 vs $0.99, so the metric tracks GAAP closely ex-charges, and coverage restores IF charges terminate) is fair but conditional on the very thing that is transcript-only. Blue also volunteered a PRO-RED correction red never made: Q2 provision $20.97M and repurchased/indemnified UPB $193.3M with $54.3M of marks are both LARGER than the thesis's $153.8M/$41.7M, loosening the ~$220M cap toward ~$250M.

=== PART 3: WHY NOT ADVANCE ON THE DRAFT ===

Blue's construction is defensible in form - business risk maps to a size cut, not a price gate, per the response taxonomy - but three things block seating it here. FIRST, the principal question is unpriced, and it is not a background risk: it is a dated, variant-selecting, front-loaded sequence that runs straight through the proposed holding period. SECOND, the tape. Verified live: last $42.56, prior close $42.78, 52w high $87.76, 52w low $41.425 - and low_13w = low_26w = low_52w = $41.425, meaning the 52-week low was set within the last 13 weeks and the name is still making lows with no base. dd52 = -51.5% and pct_off_low = +2.74% (benches said -52.5% and 3.4% off the pack's $42.78 - consistent). THIRD, and decisively: the existing ledger gate is alert_below $41.43 with gate_basis 'a 52-week-low break voids the bounded-damage premise; re-adjudicate, do not add.' Spot is 2.7% above that trigger. Seating a starter now means seating a position 2.7% from its own premise-voiding tripwire - you would buy and immediately re-adjudicate. That is not a size question, it is a construction error, and it is a stronger argument against entry than anything red filed.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION TO THE ESCALATION: NOT_YET. The ADVANCE is live and blue's gating instinct is right, but it cannot be seated until the verification pack clears - above all the primary PSPA/FHFA posture read, which determines whether the operative variant is (a) or (b), and which no amount of size-cutting substitutes for. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: KILL entry-now; blue's starter is doubly blocked (wrong-signed political risk: a Dem House removes the GOOD variant and accelerates the bad one into Sept-Dec — colliding with the proposed entry window; AND the ledger tripwire sits 2.7% away). OWED VERIFICATION (now closable via sec_fetch/FHFA): the admin's actual 2026 PSPA posture from primary — the record has none. WD|2026-11-03 = the variant-selection adjudication. || VERIFICATION PACK 8/15 (WD_VERIFICATION_20260815.md; principal's greedy question): GREEDY ENTRY BLOCKED at $42.56, conditionally licensed at $27. THE PRINCIPAL'S PREMISE VERIFIED, CONCLUSION INVERTED: privatization IS effectively far-fetched right now — PSPA un-amended, liquidation preference ACCRETING $7.6B/qtr (the barrier GROWS), zero registration statements, FHFA feed silent, Freddie's own 10-Q calls it Administration 'comments', the $30B IPO figure = vapor (Sept-2025 trade article, no government principal). Variant (c) status-quo drift CONFIRMED — the 11/03 variant pack is DOWN-WEIGHTED. But 'greedy when others are fearful' fails its own premise: THERE IS NO FEAR — short interest 3.4% falling, sell-side Buy +45.7% targets, IV at the 6th percentile nine days after a -13.9% gap. The drawdown is 75% three earnings gaps (GSE-release beta -0.021 t=-1.29 INSIGNIFICANT; political headline dates all fail event study; -17.2% since 8/5 vs peers flat) and the live deteriorating variable is CREDIT: defaults 0.07->0.28% of at-risk, Q2 provision $21M > ALL of FY25, dividend 250% H1 payout, buyback stopped w/ cash falling. ALSO: pack refuted the court's own two strongest kills from primary ($14.4B DUS = gross vs 0.3bp loss history + flat CECL; 'circular adjusted core' backwards — WD's non-GAAP is MORE conservative than peers) and corrected its own book-value signal (2.01x TANGIBLE book; 0.83x was 59%-goodwill artifact). Issuer honesty: CLEAN.
